name: Mission Control HQ
tagline: A single dashboard that pulls projects, tasks and status updates into one place so you stop opening six tabs.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible product here is a rollup view: projects, owners, statuses, deadlines, a bit of AI summarizing on top. That view is not hard to build, an agent can give you a local SQLite app with a kanban, a portfolio table and a weekly digest in one sitting. The part that does not fall out of a one-shot is where the data comes from: these tools earn their keep by sucking state out of GitHub, Jira, Linear, Slack and calendars and keeping it fresh, and every one of those is an OAuth app, a webhook endpoint and a sync loop you now own. If you are one person and willing to type your own status updates, the DIY version is genuinely fine. If the point was that the dashboard fills itself in from other people's work, you are building a small integrations company.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-user work dashboard with projects, tasks, statuses and dates, a kanban plus portfolio table, and a generated weekly review of what moved and what slipped.
requirements: Node 20 and a place to run it, a laptop is fine
An LLM API key if you want the generated weekly summary, otherwise it is template text
Discipline to actually update statuses by hand, since nothing syncs them for you
whatYouLose: Automatic sync from GitHub, Jira, Linear, Slack and calendars, which is most of the real value
Multiple people looking at the same board without you inventing auth and permissions
Push notifications and email digests that arrive whether or not you remember to open the app
Mobile access that is not just a cramped browser tab
Someone else's opinionated workflow, which is sometimes worth paying for when yours is a mess
moatNotes: The dashboard is the demo, the connectors are the product. Nobody churns because the kanban was ugly, they churn because the sync broke.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a rollup nobody updates is worse than no rollup at all. Paid tools in this slot maintain dozens of brittle integrations, handle token refresh and rate limits, and put the same numbers in front of a whole team with an audit trail. A personal build gives you the layout and the calm, but you are the sync engine, and that job gets old around week three unless you genuinely enjoy it.
notes: Fine solo, painful the moment a second human needs to see it.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user work dashboard called Mission Control. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router and TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling, no component library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/mc.db, schema created on first run
- Server Actions for all writes, no separate API layer
- Run with `npm run dev` on localhost, nothing else required

Data model:
- project: id, name, area, status (green | yellow | red), owner, due_date, notes (markdown), archived
- task: id, project_id, title, state (todo | doing | blocked | done), priority (1-3), due_date, updated_at
- update: id, project_id, body, created_at (manual status notes, append only)

Screens:
1. Portfolio: sortable table of active projects with status pill, owner, due date, count of open tasks, days since last update. Highlight rows with no update in 7+ days.
2. Board: kanban of tasks across all projects, four columns by state, drag to move, filter by project and priority.
3. Project detail: editable fields, markdown notes with preview, task list, timeline of updates.
4. Review: pick a date range, generate a digest of what changed (tasks completed, statuses that flipped, projects that went stale). Use a plain template by default. If OPENAI_API_KEY is set in .env.local, send the same facts to the model for a tighter prose summary. Never fail if the key is missing.

Also include:
- Keyboard-first quick add: press `n` anywhere, type "project: task title !2 due friday", parse it
- Export everything to JSON and import it back, one button each
- Seed script with three fake projects and about twenty tasks so the UI is not empty

Explicitly out of scope: authentication, multi-user, GitHub or Jira or Slack sync, webhooks, email, mobile app, real-time collaboration, Docker. Do not stub these with fake buttons.

When done, print a short README covering setup, the .env.local keys, and where the database file lives.
